definitions.text: Warning signs are displayed when unusual hazards, hazardous materials, hazardous equipment or special conditions are expected.
Chemicals that cause a sudden release of pressure, gas and heat when they experience sudden shock are called explosive chemicals.
Flammable chemicals or mixtures are those which have a flashpoint around room temperature.
Corrosive chemicals attack living tissues when they come in contact with them.
A toxic chemical is a poisonous material which is capable of causing serious health problems.
When a person is exposed to a high dose of radiation, it can damage the functioning of tissues and organs and can cause vomiting, radiation burns, hair loss and radiation syndrome.
It is a type of hazard in which a gas or vapours can cause unconscience or death through suffocation.
While mixing concentrated acids with water, always add acid slowly to water and not vice versa.

fullMarks: Write the hazard’s exact definition first, then give suitable examples from the chapter.
For a question asking for precautions, give separate, numbered actions that directly address the hazard.
For an emergency response, write the steps in a clear order: stay calm, alert people, take the relevant safety action, and call or assist emergency staff.
When explaining a hazard sign, state what danger it warns about and what precaution the sign calls for.
For acid dilution, state the rule clearly: add acid slowly to water, never water to acid.
There are no numerical calculations or formulas in this chapter; do not add irrelevant working or units.
The supplied 2027 paper pattern lists Units 1–11 and gives no examinable exercise references for this unit, so confirm whether this chapter is included before prioritising it for the exam.
mistakes: Writing that water should be added to concentrated acid. Fix: write that acid is added slowly to water, not vice versa.
Giving only one precaution when a question asks for several. Fix: list distinct, relevant precautions in numbered points.
Confusing corrosive and toxic hazards. Fix: corrosive chemicals attack living tissues on contact; toxic chemicals are poisonous and can cause serious health problems.
Saying that all radiation exposure has the same effect. Fix: name the listed effects of high-dose exposure, such as radiation burns and damage to tissues and organs.
Forgetting to mention ventilation when describing precautions for toxic or asphyxiant chemicals. Fix: include a well-ventilated area or a fume hood where relevant.
Giving an incomplete emergency response by describing only the fire. Fix: include alerting people, using the extinguisher where appropriate, and calling or assisting emergency staff.
